beats.care: If your PG or flat runs on a borewell, it may dry up sooner in summer, meaning costly tankers and higher bills.
beats.what: The 2025-26 groundwater assessment rates 8 Hyderabad areas over-exploited and 7 critical, up from 11 such areas a year earlier.
beats.why: Piped water covers only about 30% of demand, so homes, hostels and offices lean on borewells, while concrete stops rain soaking in.

cards.body: Over-exploited: Amberpet, Ameerpet, Asifnagar, Charminar, Golconda, Himayatnagar, Khairatabad and Saidabad. Critical: Bahadurpura, Bandlaguda, Maredpally, Musheerabad, Nampally, Secunderabad and Shaikpet. A Telangana groundwater official shared the figures.
The same region holds nearly a third of the state's people, which is why the pressure is so high.
cards.caption: Hyderabad region's share of Telangana groundwater

cards.body: Critical means an area uses 90 to 100% of the groundwater it can safely pull out each year. Over-exploited means it uses more than 100%, eating into reserves.
cards.title: what's the difference between critical and over-exploited?

cards.body: The wider core urban region still uses only about two-thirds of its yearly groundwater. It is the older, dense city core that has run out of room.

cards.q: Should borewells in red zones be restricted?

opts: Heavy borewell use and less rain soaking in
cards.q: Why is Hyderabad's groundwater running low?
cards.why: Borewells pull water out faster than concrete-covered ground lets rain refill it.

hook: Hyderabad pumps *more water than rain puts back*. Is your area listed?

learn.t: 'Over-exploited' means an area pumps out more groundwater each year than rain puts back, so the water table keeps falling.

sources.name: The Siasat Daily
sources.title: Eight Hyderabad areas over-exploit groundwater, 7 turn critical

tldr: A 2025-26 assessment finds Hyderabad district now pumps out more groundwater than rain puts back each year, with 15 of 16 areas critical or over-exploited.
